body: What you want and what you'll let yourself have pull against each other, and it shows up in who you pick. Distance may feel familiar in love. You may be drawn to people or bonds where affection has to be worked for, waited for, or proven over time. Or you become that for someone else. Affection may feel harder to trust when it comes easily. Love can seem more real when it has been tested, withheld, or earned. The see-saw plays out in relationships: you want warmth, you may choose someone who rations it, then you call the struggle proof it's real. Struggle can start to look like proof when love has often come with distance or delay. Part of you may want love to feel simpler, steadier, and easier to receive, and the work is trusting it when it finally arrives.
gift: At your best: loyal, grounded, able to build something that lasts.
shadow: The trap: picking the withholders, then mistaking the ache for love.
integration: Let standards protect your heart without closing it. Reliability matters, but so does letting tenderness arrive in ordinary moments.
do: Let love be easy and trust it
Notice if you keep choosing the unavailable
Choose the steady one even when calm feels foreign
dont: Earn affection you should just receive
Confuse the ache with the bond
